git.gitignore_content:
# Framework Research Project
# ================================================================================
# Pattern-based gitignore - works regardless of directory structure customization.
# This is the standard template for non-sensitive projects.
# ================================================================================

# ============================================================================
# PRIVATE DATA - NEVER COMMIT
# ============================================================================

# Private directories (anywhere in project tree)
**/private/**
**/*_private/**

# ============================================================================
# SECRETS AND CREDENTIALS - NEVER COMMIT
# ============================================================================

.env
.env.local
.env.*.local
.Renviron
.httr-oauth
**/credentials/**
**/secrets/**
*.key
*.pem

# ============================================================================
# UTILITY & CACHE - SAFE TO IGNORE
# ============================================================================

# Temporary processing directories
**/cache/**
**/scratch/**
**/tmp/**
**/temp/**

# Logs (run logs, cluster job output)
**/logs/**
slurm-*.out

# ============================================================================
# FRAMEWORK INTERNALS
# ============================================================================

framework.db
framework.db-wal
framework.db-shm
.initiated
.framework_scaffolded

# ============================================================================
# QUARTO ARTIFACTS
# ============================================================================

# Quarto adds these two lines, in this form, unless they are here already
/.quarto/
**/*.quarto_ipynb
# A folder with its own _quarto.yml gets its own .quarto/
.quarto/
_freeze/
# Backups from quarto_regenerate() before framework-py 0.1.0.dev13
.quarto_backups/
*_cache/
*_files/

# ============================================================================
# PYTHON ENVIRONMENT
# ============================================================================

__pycache__/
*.py[cod]
.venv/
venv/
.ipynb_checkpoints/
.pytest_cache/
.mypy_cache/
.ruff_cache/
*.egg-info/
build/
dist/

# ============================================================================
# IDE & SYSTEM FILES
# ============================================================================

# IDE - personal settings only (commit workspace settings if desired)
.idea/
.vscode/.history/
.positron/.history/
.history/

# macOS
.DS_Store
.AppleDouble
.LSOverride

# Windows
Thumbs.db
ehthumbs.db

# Linux
*~

# ============================================================================
# TEMPORARY FILES
# ============================================================================

*.tmp
*.log
*.bak
*.swp
*~

# --- from base framework/shiny_python v2 ---
# Private data and credentials
**/private/**
**/*_private/**
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
.Renviron
**/credentials/**
**/secrets/**

# Local records and caches
framework.db
framework.db-wal
framework.db-shm
.DS_Store

# Python environments and caches
.venv/
__pycache__/
.pytest_cache/
rsconnect-python/

git-workflow.content:
---
name: git-workflow
description: Use when reviewing changes, committing analysis work, resolving merge conflicts, or coordinating branches in a research repository.
metadata:
  title: Using Git in an analysis project
  summary: Reviewable Git changes for analysis code and project files.
---

# Using Git in an analysis project

## Changes

- Check the branch, status, and diff before editing or committing.
- Keep unrelated work as it is.
- Stage explicit paths, so generated output, data, credentials, and
  machine-specific files stay out of commits.
- Keep each commit to one coherent change, and describe what changed.

## Conflicts

- Resolve notebook conflicts with notebook-aware tools when available.
- Regenerate generated files from their source.
- Rerun affected analyses after resolving a conflict.

## Shared history

- Leave shared history as it is. Check divergence before merging or rebasing.
- Commit, push, and publish only when the user asks.
